# Browser Testing Gotchas

> Known browser testing and pointer event patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Pointer event handoff between trigger and popup requires explicit handling](pointer-event-relatedtarget.md): Chromium sends mouseout after pointerleave even within the same layout; check relatedTarget to know if pointer entered a related element. MEDIUM.
- [Browser tests miss rendering-order and lazy-stylesheet bugs](browser-tests-visual-vs-markup.md): DOM tests pass for unstyled markup; lazy-loaded stylesheets, computed layout, and text wrapping require visual harnesses with real browser rendering. HIGH.
- [Mobile audit evidence must wait for loaded content](browser-audit-loaded-content.md): An audit check that runs before content populates measures the loading placeholder, so a non-empty "Loading" state reads as ready and the check passes on the wrong UI; wait for a loaded-content signal, not for a non-empty element. HIGH.
- [Ctrl-wheel zoom does not prove two-touch pinch](ctrl-wheel-zoom-does-not-prove-two-touch-pinch.md): Desktop trackpad pinch can exercise only the ctrl+wheel path while a touch-action-none surface has no real two-contact implementation; verify with two independently identified touch contacts. HIGH.
- [Pre-event snapshots cannot prove post-event cancellation](pre-event-snapshots-cannot-prove-post-event-cancellation.md): A repeating animation frame may run between a state read and asynchronous input delivery; snapshot after cancellation is observed, then prove the state stays fixed. MEDIUM.
- [Persist measurement evidence before enforcing thresholds](persist-measurement-evidence-before-enforcing-thresholds.md): Write raw samples before assertions, attach structured failure data, and upload artifacts on every outcome so a red performance gate remains diagnosable. MEDIUM.
- [Physical screen size does not prove the CSS viewport](physical-screen-size-does-not-prove-the-css-viewport.md): Browser chrome, display scaling and page zoom can cross a height breakpoint on a large monitor, leaving successful actions hidden in a fallback presentation. HIGH.
